title: Facebook Ads Audit Checklist
description: Audit a Facebook or Instagram account from business outcome back to the ad. A low cost per lead is useful only when those leads can become customers.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Audit a Facebook or Instagram account from business outcome back to the ad. A low cost per lead is useful only when those leads can become customers.

sections.title: Start with a reliable comparison
body: Export two comparable reporting periods and write down the campaign objective, attribution setting, spend and business outcome. Mark promotions, stock changes and tracking releases that could distort the comparison. Separate new-customer acquisition from remarketing.
bullets: Account: confirm the business owns the ad account, billing and connected assets; remove access that is no longer needed.
Measurement: complete a test enquiry or purchase and compare the event with the actual CRM record or order.
Offer: open every destination on a phone and confirm the price, promise and next step match the ad.
Delivery: review spend, reach, frequency and conversions by campaign before drilling into placements or creatives.

sections.title: Build a useful issue register
body: For each finding record evidence, likely impact, an owner and the next check. “Tracking problem” is too vague; “purchase fires again when the receipt page reloads” is an actionable defect. Fix invalid measurement before reallocating budget.
bullets: Example: 40 recorded leads but only 25 unique enquiries means the reported CPL cannot be trusted yet.
Example: an ad gets clicks but the contact button fails on Android. Repair the destination before commissioning new creative.

sections.title: Finish with decisions
body: Choose three priority changes, keep a dated log and define what would count as improvement. Compare qualified enquiries and customer acquisition cost after enough outcomes have accumulated. Avoid declaring a winner from one sale or changing every variable at once. An audit should leave an evidence trail, not a long list of unexplained dashboard scores.

sections.title: Check the lead behind the green dashboard
body: Start with the last ten enquiries the business actually received. Match each to its campaign where attribution is available, then check whether the phone number worked, the requirement fit and someone followed up. Ten records are a troubleshooting sample, not enough to estimate a stable conversion rate. They can still reveal an obvious defect that a campaign average hides.

For example, an enquiry for a service you do not offer may come from an ambiguous ad rather than poor targeting. Read the ad and form together. If the ad says ‘website from ₹5,000’ and the salesperson quotes a much larger minimum, the expectation gap starts before the lead arrives. Fix the promise or explain the limited scope clearly.

sections.title: Separate urgent repairs from experiments
body: Broken destinations, duplicate purchase events, wrong service areas and ads for unavailable products need immediate attention. A new headline or a different image is an experiment. Putting both in the same priority list makes it easy to spend a week testing creative while a checkout remains broken.

Write the issue as an observation: ‘The thank-you page records a lead on every refresh.’ Add the affected URL, device, reproduction steps and a proposed verification. After the repair, submit one labelled test enquiry and confirm that it creates one business record and the intended measurement event. Keep personal details out of audit screenshots.

sections.title: What to hand over after the audit
body: The deliverable should include the reporting dates, the account and campaigns reviewed, unresolved questions, and a short list of actions with owners. Keep the original export so later comparisons use the same metric definitions. If the business cannot supply sales outcomes, say that the audit assessed lead generation rather than profitability.

Agree the next review around the sales cycle. A home renovation enquiry that closes after several weeks cannot be fairly compared with an immediate online purchase. Record late outcomes against the period that generated the lead instead of assuming every unclosed enquiry has failed.

title: Facebook Ads Cost in India: Plan Your Budget
description: Plan your Facebook Ads budget in India. Understand ad spend, management fees, creative costs, and the sales numbers that make a campaign viable.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Facebook Ads has no universal price per customer in India. Separate the amount paid to Meta from creative production, campaign management and the cost of converting enquiries into sales.

sections.title: Build the budget from unit economics
body: Write down contribution per sale after fulfilment and the portion you can allocate to acquisition. Use the close rate from your own sales records to translate an affordable customer cost into an affordable qualified-lead cost.
bullets: Media budget: money spent inside the advertising account.
Production: images, edits, scripts and landing-page work.
Management: setup, optimisation and reporting fees.
Other costs: tools, applicable taxes and any agreed integrations.

sections.title: An illustrative calculation
body: Suppose a sale contributes ₹4,000 before acquisition, and the business chooses a ₹1,000 acquisition ceiling. If one in ten qualified enquiries becomes a sale, an initial qualified-lead ceiling is ₹100. At a ₹10,000 media budget, that model needs 100 qualified enquiries and ten sales to meet the ceiling. These are planning assumptions, not Indian market averages or a ReddyStack quote.

sections.title: How to use early campaign data
body: Record raw leads, duplicates, qualified leads and completed sales separately. If raw leads cost ₹50 but only one quarter qualify, the qualified-lead cost is ₹200. Recalculate the budget using that number and the observed close rate. Ask a provider which costs are included, who owns the account and how overspend is handled. A cheap click does not establish a profitable campaign.

sections.title: Work backwards from one sale
body: Suppose a service sale brings in ₹8,000 and the direct cost of delivering it is ₹5,000. That leaves ₹3,000 before advertising, overhead and profit. If only one in ten qualified enquiries becomes a customer, spending ₹300 per qualified enquiry would use the whole ₹3,000 contribution. It would not leave money for management fees or profit. This is an illustrative calculation, not a claim about typical Indian campaign costs.

Use your own numbers and allow for cancellations. If you do not know the close rate yet, calculate a cautious and an optimistic scenario. The difference shows how much you are assuming before spending real money.

sections.title: Ask what is included in the fee
body: Two management quotes may cover very different work. One may include campaign setup and a monthly report; another may include creative production, landing-page changes and a connection to your lead system. Compare the number of campaigns, creative variations, reporting work and revision rounds before comparing the total price.
bullets: Who pays Meta, and does the business retain billing access?
Are design, video editing and copy included or quoted separately?
Who repairs the website if conversion tracking or the form fails?
What happens to the account and source files when the engagement ends?

sections.title: A lower lead price can cost more overall
body: Imagine two tests costing ₹10,000 each. The first brings 100 enquiries, of which five are suitable. The second brings 40 enquiries, of which ten are suitable. Raw lead costs are ₹100 and ₹250; suitable-lead costs are ₹2,000 and ₹1,000. The second test also asks the sales team to process fewer unsuitable enquiries.

Keep media spend, agency or freelancer fees, and sales handling costs visible separately. Once tracking is reliable, use that complete picture to decide what you can afford. A screenshot of a low CPL is not enough to judge whether a campaign is commercially workable.

title: Facebook Ads Budget for a Small Business
description: Set a practical Facebook Ads budget for your small business. Plan a focused test, estimate lead costs, and decide when to adjust campaign spend.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: A small-business ad budget should buy a focused learning test that the business can afford. Start with one offer and a clear customer outcome before splitting spend across many campaigns.

sections.title: Set a test you can interpret
body: Choose the audience, location, offer, conversion action and sales follow-up owner. Establish a maximum test loss and a review date. If the proposed budget is too small to generate meaningful outcomes at your expected lead cost, narrow the test rather than spreading the same amount across more ad sets.
bullets: Use a fixed planning period and a written media-spend limit.
Keep production and management fees outside the media calculation.
Choose a qualified-lead or purchase target, not only a click target.
Reserve time for follow-up; unanswered enquiries waste paid demand.

sections.title: Use a sensitivity range
body: Illustrative model: a ₹6,000 test buys 120, 60 or 30 leads at assumed CPLs of ₹50, ₹100 or ₹200. At a 20% qualification rate those become 24, 12 or 6 qualified leads. The exercise shows how uncertain the result is before spending; it is not a forecast. Decide whether those possible sample sizes can answer your question.

sections.title: When to increase or stop
body: Increase spend gradually only when tracking is reliable, delivery capacity exists and qualified outcomes justify the change. Pause for broken checkout, misdirected enquiries or uncontrolled spend. Poor results with very few leads may remain inconclusive; document that instead of declaring that the channel never works. Repeat a controlled test when the offer or measurement has materially improved.

sections.title: Choose the question your budget should answer
body: ‘Will advertising work?’ is too broad for a first test. A better question is whether one clearly described service can attract suitable enquiries in the area you serve. Pick a service with available capacity, a landing page that explains it and someone who can respond. If the service cannot be delivered for several weeks, decide how that delay will be communicated before the campaign starts.

Keep a short test brief: the offer, audience, destination, success event, amount you can afford to lose and the decision date. There is no universal test budget that produces a reliable answer for every business.

sections.title: Do not divide a small budget into too many pieces
body: A test split across six services, four locations and several creative ideas may leave each combination with very little evidence. A handful of clicks per version cannot tell you which offer attracts customers. Consolidate around the business question first, then introduce another variable when the first test has produced useful information.

Set aside the time and cost of creating at least one genuinely different message. Replacing a blue background with a green one is less informative than comparing a demonstration of the service with an explanation of the problem it solves. Keep the destination and qualification criteria steady when comparing those messages.

sections.title: Keep a spending and response log
body: Record daily spend, enquiries received, enquiries contacted and qualified outcomes. Add notes when the phone was unanswered, stock ran out or the website was unavailable. Those interruptions affect the test and should not disappear inside an average.

At the review, choose among three conclusions: the test supports another controlled step, a specific defect needs repair, or the evidence is still too limited. If you increase the budget, confirm that response capacity increases with it. Buying more leads while yesterday’s enquiries remain untouched creates a sales problem that new targeting cannot solve.

title: How to Diagnose Low-Quality Facebook Leads
description: Cheap Facebook leads can become expensive sales work. Diagnose where relevance breaks down before adding more form fields or changing the audience.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Cheap Facebook leads can become expensive sales work. Diagnose where relevance breaks down before adding more form fields or changing the audience.

sections.title: Define the problem in the CRM
body: Classify a sample of recent enquiries as duplicate, unreachable, outside service area, unsuitable requirement, wrong budget, qualified or customer. Use the same labels across campaigns and record when each lead received its first response. “Bad lead” alone hides problems that require different fixes.
bullets: Outside area: compare the promised coverage with delivery and location settings.
Wrong expectation: inspect the ad promise, sample pricing language and landing page.
Unreachable: check accidental submissions, contact validation and response timing.
Unsuitable need: add one question that changes whether you can serve the enquiry.

sections.title: Change the signal, not just the volume
body: Illustrative example: campaign A generates 50 enquiries with five qualified; campaign B produces 25 with ten qualified at the same spend. Campaign B has the higher raw CPL but the lower qualified CPL. Judge the campaign against the qualification definition, not the form-submission count. Only send eligible customer data back to platforms through an agreed, privacy-aware measurement setup.

sections.title: A controlled next test
body: Keep the offer and sales response process stable. Test a clearer price boundary or a service-area statement, then compare qualification rate and qualified-lead cost. Too much friction can exclude suitable buyers as well, so also review form completion. Keep useful business questions and remove questions that nobody uses to make a decision.

sections.title: Read what people thought they were requesting
body: Ask the person handling enquiries to record the first question each lead asks. Repeated questions about a free service, a job opening or a price you never offered often point to misleading context. Read the creative as someone who has never heard of your business. A short form and an attractive image can make the intended service less obvious than the campaign owner expects.

For an illustrative cleaning business, ‘Get your free home assessment’ could be understood as free cleaning. ‘Request a quote for paid home cleaning in these areas’ is less ambiguous. The clearer version may generate fewer forms while saving hours of irrelevant calls.

sections.title: Use questions that change your next action
body: A useful form question helps you route or qualify the request. Service location, required work and an approximate start date can be more helpful than a long open-ended biography. Explain why sensitive or unusual information is needed, and avoid collecting it when it does not affect the initial conversation.

Do not add five compulsory fields simply because lead quality is poor. You may exclude suitable customers who are using a phone or do not yet know the terminology. Test one meaningful qualifier and compare suitable enquiries per rupee as well as form completion.

sections.title: Check the follow-up process separately
body: An unanswered call does not prove that someone was a fake lead. Record how long the first response took, the permitted contact channel and the outcome of the follow-up. If staff call from different numbers or cannot explain which offer the person saw, a genuine prospect may be confused.

Keep the classification simple enough to use consistently: outside area, wrong service, duplicate, unreachable, qualified and won. Review examples of each label together. A campaign cannot optimise around ‘quality’ if salespeople use that word to mean six different things. Share only the customer information that the business is authorised to use for measurement.

title: Meta Pixel vs Conversions API
description: Meta Pixel and Conversions API are two routes for sending measurement events to Meta. Choose the setup by the events your business needs and the systems you can maintain.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Meta Pixel and Conversions API are two routes for sending measurement events to Meta. Choose the setup by the events your business needs and the systems you can maintain.

sections.title: Understand the event journey
body: A browser event is triggered on the visitor’s device. A server event is sent from a connected backend or integration. The same purchase can travel through both routes, so the measurement design needs a way to recognise that they describe one action. Server-side collection does not remove privacy or consent obligations.
bullets: List each business event and the system that knows it really happened.
Decide which events are browser-based, server-based or both.
Document event names, identifiers, timestamps, currency and value where relevant.
Keep credentials server-side and limit access to the integration.

sections.title: Validate one complete transaction
body: Use a clearly identified test order. Check the browser event, the server event and the order record. Where both routes report the action, verify event matching and deduplication using Meta’s current documentation. Reload the confirmation page and retry a webhook to check whether the order is incorrectly counted twice. Never assume an installed plugin proves the setup is correct.

sections.title: Which should a small business choose?
body: A supported platform integration can be easier to operate than custom code. A custom integration makes sense when important events happen in a backend that the standard connector cannot cover. Define an owner for failures and retest after checkout or consent changes. CAPI improves the available measurement path; it does not guarantee perfect attribution or permission to send every customer field.

sections.title: Start with the system that knows the action happened
body: A click on ‘Pay’ only shows an attempt. The order system knows whether payment succeeded. A form submit button similarly does not prove that the enquiry reached the business. Write down the point at which each event becomes true before choosing a browser tag or server integration.

For a purchase, useful fields can include a stable order or event identifier, the event time, currency and the value defined by your reporting rules. Decide how refunds, cancelled orders and test purchases will be recognised. Otherwise a technically working integration can still produce a misleading sales report.

sections.title: Give duplicate delivery a predictable outcome
body: Browsers can reload and backend systems can retry. If both paths describe the same completed purchase, the receiving platform needs a consistent way to recognise that overlap. Check Meta’s current event matching and deduplication instructions for your integration rather than guessing from similar names in two dashboards.

Keep a small test record containing the order reference, event identifier and expected result. Send the same transaction through the intended paths, refresh the receipt page and inspect the resulting count. Then test a genuinely different order. The goal is to count the repeated delivery once while still counting two separate purchases twice.

sections.title: Plan for consent and maintenance
body: Server-side delivery is not a way to ignore the visitor’s privacy choices. Map those choices through the browser, order system and integration. Do not send message text, payment credentials or an entire customer record because an integration accepts additional fields.

Prefer a supported integration when it covers the events you need and you can see its errors. Assign responsibility for checking failures after changes to checkout, forms or consent settings. Better coverage is useful, but it does not make platform attribution a complete record of why every customer bought. Reconcile it with business records.

title: Facebook Ads vs Google Ads: Choosing a Starting Channel
description: Compare Facebook Ads and Google Ads by search demand, creative needs, and buying intent. Choose a starting channel that fits your business.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Choose between Meta and Google Ads by how customers discover and buy your offer. Search demand, creative assets and sales economics matter more than a generic claim that one channel is cheaper.

sections.title: Compare the buying situation
body: Google Search can reach people expressing a need through a query. Facebook and Instagram can introduce an offer while someone is browsing. Both platforms have additional formats, so this distinction is a starting point rather than a description of every campaign type.
bullets: Known problem and urgent enquiry: investigate relevant Search demand and landing-page fit.
Visually demonstrable product: consider whether a social ad can communicate value quickly.
Unfamiliar offer: plan education before expecting a direct purchase.
Limited budget: choose one clear test rather than underfunding both channels.

sections.title: Make the comparison fair
body: An illustrative service business might compare search enquiries and social enquiries after using the same qualification definition, service area and response process. Keep platform-reported conversions visible, but reconcile sales in the CRM. A platform may attribute the same customer differently; adding both reported totals can overstate business results.

sections.title: Decide using evidence
body: Estimate demand and costs before launch, then review qualified customer cost, contribution after acquisition and operational capacity. Search may be constrained by available demand; social may require more creative iteration. Use the stronger channel as a starting point and add the other only when it has a defined role. A retargeting campaign is not a substitute for a plan to acquire new demand.

sections.title: Compare two different buying situations
body: Someone searching for an emergency plumber has already named a problem. The ad and landing page need to confirm coverage, availability and how to make contact. A new handmade homeware collection may need photographs or a demonstration before a person realises they want it. These are examples of buying situations, not rules that all service businesses belong on Google or all products belong on Instagram.

Look for evidence of existing demand, including relevant search queries and the questions customers already ask. Also inspect whether you have persuasive creative assets. A channel decision should reflect what the business can communicate well today.

sections.title: Compare equivalent outcomes
body: Do not compare a Meta form submission with a Google purchase and call the cheaper one the winner. Write a shared definition of a qualified enquiry or completed order. Keep service area, price, landing-page quality and response standards comparable. Record channel-specific differences that cannot reasonably be held constant.

A buyer may see a social ad, later search for the brand and eventually contact the business directly. Separate platform attribution from a deduplicated list of customers. Asking ‘How did you hear about us?’ can add context, but people may not remember every touchpoint.

sections.title: Decide what would justify a second channel
body: A second channel needs a role: reaching additional relevant demand, explaining a visual product, or answering questions for people who have already visited. It also needs enough budget and operating attention. Adding it solely because a competitor advertises there creates more reporting work without a clear hypothesis.

If the first channel produces useful enquiries but sales are weak, inspect price, qualification and follow-up before buying more traffic elsewhere. If demand is limited despite sound economics, a different channel may be worth testing. State that reason in the brief so the eventual review can answer the original question.

title: Facebook Ads for Ecommerce: A Launch Checklist
description: An ecommerce campaign needs more than product images. Make the offer, catalogue, checkout and purchase measurement agree before sending paid traffic.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: An ecommerce campaign needs more than product images. Make the offer, catalogue, checkout and purchase measurement agree before sending paid traffic.

sections.title: Check the store first
body: Buy a test item using a phone, including a variant and delivery address. Confirm that the price, availability, shipping cost and delivery promise stay consistent from ad to receipt. Campaign optimisation cannot repair an unavailable product or an unreliable checkout.
bullets: Catalogue: accurate IDs, variants, prices, stock and destination URLs.
Creative: show the actual product and explain a specific reason to buy.
Checkout: usable payment flow, visible shipping and clear return information.
Measurement: one completed order, correct value and currency, no reload duplicates.

sections.title: Protect contribution, not only revenue
body: Illustrative example: an order worth ₹2,000 is not a ₹2,000 advertising allowance. Subtract product cost, fulfilment, payment charges, discounts and an allowance for returns to understand available contribution. Calculate acquisition economics before judging the campaign by return on ad spend alone. A high revenue ratio can still conceal weak margins.

sections.title: Plan the first review
body: Compare new and returning customers when reliable data allows it. Inspect product-level availability, returns and purchase-event integrity alongside ad performance. Pause creative for unavailable variants and make changes in the source catalogue instead of fixing each ad manually. Scale only when fulfilment, stock and customer support can handle the extra demand. Treat claimed platform revenue as an attribution view to reconcile with store records.

sections.title: Test the awkward order, not only the easy one
body: A standard test order may work while common variations fail. Try a different size, an unavailable colour, a discount code and a delivery postcode near the edge of your coverage. Check what happens when payment fails or a shopper returns from the payment provider. Use the platform’s approved test method where possible and keep test orders out of sales reporting.

Product IDs need to remain consistent between the store, catalogue and measurement system. If each integration describes the same variant differently, product-level reporting and relevant follow-up messages become harder to trust. Repair the source data before manually correcting individual ads.

sections.title: Write down the margin calculation
body: Consider an illustrative ₹2,000 order with ₹900 product cost, ₹150 fulfilment, ₹60 payment fees and a ₹100 allowance for returns. That leaves ₹790 before advertising, management costs, overhead and profit. A ₹700 acquisition cost might look acceptable beside ₹2,000 revenue, yet leave almost no room for the rest of the business.

Repeat the calculation for the products you intend to promote. A blended store average can hide a low-margin item that consumes most of the advertising budget. Treat repeat-purchase value as an assumption until your own customer records support it.

sections.title: Match creative to the reason for hesitation
body: A product demonstration can answer questions that a discount cannot: how the item fits, what is included, how it is used and what scale it is. Show the actual version being sold. Keep shipping, returns and availability consistent between the ad and product page.

After launch, review cancelled and returned orders alongside attributed purchases. An ad that overstates the product can generate sales followed by refunds and support work. The useful outcome is an order the business can fulfil and the customer wants to keep.

title: A Practical Facebook Retargeting Strategy
description: Retargeting should answer the question that stopped a relevant visitor from buying. Define the audience, message and exclusion rules before deciding how often to show the ad.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Retargeting should answer the question that stopped a relevant visitor from buying. Define the audience, message and exclusion rules before deciding how often to show the ad.

sections.title: Map audiences to intent
body: Someone who watched a short video has shown a different signal from someone who started checkout. Design the message around the event and its recency, and use only audience data that your business is permitted to use.
bullets: Product viewer: clarify product use, suitability or an important feature.
Checkout starter: explain delivery, payment or return information without inventing urgency.
Service-page visitor: answer a buying objection or show relevant project evidence.
Recent customer: exclude from acquisition messaging unless there is a suitable repeat-purchase offer.

sections.title: Write the sequence before launch
body: For an illustrative online course, the first reminder might explain who the course fits, and the next could clarify time commitment. Repeating “buy now” to everyone does not address either question. Set audience windows around the actual purchase cycle and available audience size. Avoid very small segments that cannot support useful delivery.

sections.title: Watch for diminishing value
body: Review reach, frequency, qualified outcomes and the incremental role of retargeting. A person already close to buying may convert after seeing an ad, but attribution alone does not prove the ad caused the sale. Where scale permits, use a suitable holdout or platform experiment. Exclude converted customers reliably and refresh the message when it no longer resolves a real objection.

sections.title: Make the reminder useful on its own
body: A person who looked at a service page may still need to know what is included, how long their part of the process takes or whether the service fits their business. A reminder can answer one of those questions directly. Avoid copy that implies you know private details about the individual or makes the visitor feel watched.

For an illustrative website project, one message might show the content a customer needs to supply. Another could explain what happens to domain ownership at handover. Neither needs an invented countdown or a discount that the business does not normally offer.

sections.title: Check whether the audience is usable
body: Very small groups may not support consistent delivery or a meaningful comparison. Start with an audience definition that relates to a real decision, then assess the available size and current platform requirements. Dividing a small website audience into many narrow recency windows can make the plan harder to operate without producing better evidence.

Define exclusions before launch. A recent buyer should not keep receiving the same first-purchase offer unless the product and timing make sense. Check how quickly completed purchases reach the audience system. Delayed or missing events can make an otherwise sensible exclusion unreliable.

sections.title: Ask whether the ads added anything
body: Retargeting often reaches people who were already close to buying. A high attributed return therefore does not establish that all those orders depended on the reminder. Where traffic and platform tools allow, compare against a suitable holdout or experiment. With a small audience, acknowledge that you may not be able to measure the extra effect precisely.

Watch spend, reach, frequency and verified outcomes together. Rising frequency with little new reach and no improvement in outcomes is a reason to inspect the message and budget, not an automatic reason to keep spending because the audience once showed interest.

title: Meta Ads Reporting Metrics That Support Decisions
description: A useful Meta Ads report connects spending with business outcomes and a next action. Keep platform delivery metrics and verified sales outcomes visible as different layers.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: A useful Meta Ads report connects spending with business outcomes and a next action. Keep platform delivery metrics and verified sales outcomes visible as different layers.

sections.title: Use a compact reporting sheet
body: Record the reporting window, currency and attribution setting at the top. Compare equivalent periods and annotate tracking changes, promotions and stock issues before interpreting movement.
bullets: Delivery: spend, impressions, reach and frequency.
Response: link clicks, landing-page visits and relevant engagement.
Conversion: leads or purchases with the event definition stated.
Business: unique qualified leads, completed sales, revenue and contribution where available.

sections.title: Calculate the right denominator
body: CPL = spend divided by leads. Qualified CPL = spend divided by qualified leads. Customer acquisition cost = the defined acquisition spend divided by new customers. In an example with ₹10,000 spent, 100 leads and 20 qualified leads, CPL is ₹100 while qualified CPL is ₹500. Label the spend included in each calculation so media-only and fully loaded costs are not confused.

sections.title: Turn the report into an action
body: State one finding, its evidence, an uncertainty and an owner. For example, “qualified CPL rose while raw CPL stayed flat; review lead rejection reasons before increasing spend.” Do not add platform totals together as unique customers without deduplication. A tidy report should make the next decision easier, not bury it beneath screenshots or a single blended efficiency score.

sections.title: Build a report somebody can reconcile
body: Begin with spend and a list of real enquiries or orders for the same reporting period. State the account time zone, currency and attribution settings. If one report counts the date of the click and another the date of the sale, a day-by-day comparison may disagree even when both systems are working.

Keep a separate column for unresolved records. Do not quietly turn missing information into zero revenue or a rejected lead. Report how much of the outcome data is complete so the reader knows whether a profitability conclusion is justified.

sections.title: Explain changes with the right companion metric
body: A falling cost per click might indicate more appealing creative, but it could also reflect less valuable traffic. Read it with landing-page visits and qualified outcomes. Rising frequency might mean you are repeatedly reaching a small audience; inspect reach and the purchase cycle before labelling it fatigue.

Use a simple reporting sentence: ‘Spend increased, suitable enquiries stayed flat, and outside-area enquiries grew.’ That observation suggests checking coverage and message clarity. ‘Performance improved by 20%’ is not useful until the metric, denominator and comparison dates are clear.

sections.title: Show the decision and the uncertainty
body: A useful weekly note contains the change made, the evidence observed and the next action. If only two purchases occurred, say that the sample is too small for a confident creative comparison. Keep a promising result visible without turning it into a guarantee.

For sales that close later, update earlier lead cohorts rather than comparing yesterday’s unresolved enquiries with last month’s completed sales. Maintain one deduplicated customer total in the business records. Platform reports remain useful views of attribution, but their totals should not be added together as if they represented different people.

title: Facebook Ads Not Converting? Diagnose the Funnel
description: When Facebook Ads generate clicks without enquiries or purchases, inspect the whole conversion journey. Increasing spend before finding the broken step can magnify the problem.
subtitle: Meta Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: When Facebook Ads generate clicks without enquiries or purchases, inspect the whole conversion journey. Increasing spend before finding the broken step can magnify the problem.

sections.title: Trace one visitor journey
body: Open the actual ad destination on a phone. Confirm the page loads, the offer matches, the form works and the confirmation reaches the business. Then check whether the platform records that real action. Separate a lack of customers from a lack of tracking.
bullets: Few impressions: inspect account, ad approval and delivery conditions.
Impressions without useful clicks: review message relevance and the creative.
Clicks without landing visits: test speed, redirects and destination availability.
Visits without actions: inspect trust, offer fit and form or checkout friction.
Actions without recorded conversions: test the event definition and integration.

sections.title: Use a specific hypothesis
body: Illustrative example: 200 reported clicks but only 70 landing-page visits suggests investigating loading or measurement differences before blaming the form. If qualified enquiries exist in the CRM but the platform shows none, fixing reporting is the first task. Small samples may not distinguish a weak offer from normal variation.

sections.title: Choose one repair and verify it
body: Record the current numbers and change the most plausible issue first. Complete a test action after each technical repair. For an offer or creative test, agree the outcome and review window beforehand. Check whether the resulting leads are usable, not merely more numerous. Keep an annotated change log so future campaign reviews can connect an improvement with what actually changed.

sections.title: Find the first step that breaks
body: Follow the journey in order: ad exposure, click, page load, intended action, successful submission or payment, and business follow-up. The first material drop gives you a place to investigate. A difference between two metrics is a clue rather than proof because platforms may count clicks and visits differently.

Try the ad’s actual link on a phone using a normal connection. Check redirects, consent prompts, sticky buttons and the on-screen keyboard. A form can look fine on a desktop while a mobile visitor cannot reach the submit button or understand which field failed.

sections.title: Distinguish reporting failure from customer hesitation
body: If a completed order exists in the store but no purchase event appears, inspect measurement first. If the event fires but the order does not exist, the success condition is wrong. If neither exists, speak to a few people who reached the sales conversation and ask which question stopped them.

Typical questions are concrete: What does delivery cost? Does the service cover my area? What do I need to supply? Is the advertised price the amount I will pay? Answer the relevant question near the decision point. A larger button will not repair an offer the reader cannot understand.

sections.title: Decide when to pause
body: Pause the affected traffic when the destination is broken, a product is unavailable or the offer is materially wrong. For a working page with disappointing results, define a test before changing it. Keep the old version, record the hypothesis and decide which outcome matters.

For example, clarify the starting scope and exclusions while keeping the audience stable. Review suitable enquiries and sales workload as well as submission rate. More forms can be a worse result if they mostly come from people expecting a different service. Treat an inconclusive small test as inconclusive rather than rewriting the entire campaign every day.

title: Google Ads Audit Checklist
description: A Google Ads audit should explain which spending decisions to change and why. Start with real conversions and customer value before inspecting individual keywords.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: A Google Ads audit should explain which spending decisions to change and why. Start with real conversions and customer value before inspecting individual keywords.

sections.title: Check foundations before performance
body: Record account ownership, billing, campaign goals and the reporting period. Confirm that a primary conversion represents an outcome worth bidding towards. A page view or button click may be useful context without being an appropriate primary sales goal.
bullets: Conversion actions: verify source, counting, values and duplicate imports.
Targeting: inspect actual locations served, exclusions, schedules and languages.
Search demand: review search terms, match types and negative keywords.
Destinations: check offer consistency, phone usability and successful submission.
Budget: compare allocation with qualified outcomes rather than headline traffic.

sections.title: Trace wasted spend with evidence
body: In an illustrative account, a campaign may show cheap conversions because it counts both a lead-form event and the same lead imported from analytics. Another may attract research queries that never become qualified enquiries. Those findings need different fixes: reconcile goals in the first case and investigate intent in the second. Do not apply a bulk list of exclusions without checking what the business actually sells.

sections.title: Leave a prioritised action log
body: For every issue, include the campaign, supporting evidence, proposed change, owner and validation method. Repair measurement and broken destinations first. Then test targeting, messages and allocation. Keep the change history intact so a later review can distinguish an improvement caused by a repair from a promotion, seasonality or a different reporting window.

sections.title: Reconcile the conversions before ranking the campaigns
body: Select a few recorded conversions and trace them to actual enquiries or orders. Check whether the same action appears through a direct Google Ads tag and an Analytics import. Two functioning integrations can still describe one customer action twice. Also check whether a contact-button click is being counted alongside the successful enquiry.

Write a conversion register with the event name, source, trigger, counting rule and business meaning. The person reading the audit should be able to tell which events represent customers and which are clues about website use. A high conversion total means little when those definitions are mixed.

sections.title: Read search terms as customer requests
body: Sort the available terms by spend, then read them alongside the page and offer. A query for ‘website development course’ means something different from ‘website developer for my shop’. A business offering both training and development needs separate treatment; a business offering only development has a clearer exclusion decision.

Do not exclude every term without a sale in a short reporting window. Some searches may be relevant but have too little evidence, and some services close after a delay. Mark terms as clearly irrelevant, relevant but uncertain, or supported by suitable outcomes. That is more useful than treating every unconverted click as waste.

sections.title: Check who can act on each finding
body: A paid-search specialist may change a negative keyword but need a developer to repair the form. A business owner may need to clarify service boundaries or decide whether a low-margin offer is worth advertising. Put the responsible person next to the issue so it does not remain an observation with no route to resolution.

End with a short repair order: measurement defects, unusable destinations, wrong intent or geography, then controlled experiments. Preserve account history and before-change exports. When performance changes later, you need to know whether the cause was your repair, a promotion or an unrelated change in demand.

title: Google Ads Cost in India: Budget and Fee Planning
description: Plan Google Ads costs in India around your offer, margins, and conversion rate. Separate advertising spend, management fees, and landing-page work.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Google Ads costs depend on the auction, offer and conversion journey. Build an India campaign budget from your business economics instead of treating a quoted average CPC as a promise.

sections.title: Separate the costs
body: Use the account’s planning tools and your own history for estimates. A Keyword Difficulty score measures an SEO opportunity; it is not an advertising price or a bid recommendation.
bullets: Media spend goes to the advertising platform.
Management covers the agreed account work and reporting.
Landing pages, creative and measurement may have separate scopes.
Tools and applicable taxes should be stated in the quote.

sections.title: Translate clicks into a useful forecast
body: Illustrative assumptions: ₹20,000 media spend at ₹40 per click buys 500 clicks. At a 4% enquiry rate that yields 20 enquiries, or ₹1,000 per enquiry. If half qualify, the qualified-lead cost becomes ₹2,000. If two become customers, media acquisition cost is ₹10,000 per customer. These numbers demonstrate the calculation; they are not average costs or guaranteed results.

sections.title: Agree limits and review rules
body: Check the campaign’s average daily budget and applicable spending-limit rules before launch. A daily average should not be mistaken for a strict identical spend every day. Set reporting, alerting and approval responsibilities. Reforecast after observing conversion and qualification rates, and stop to repair tracking or a broken enquiry flow before buying more traffic. The lowest CPC is not necessarily the lowest customer cost.

sections.title: Use a range rather than one reassuring forecast
body: Keep the media budget fixed and vary one assumption. With an illustrative ₹20,000 budget and ₹40 CPC, 500 clicks at a 2% enquiry rate produce ten enquiries; at 4%, they produce twenty. Media cost per enquiry changes from ₹2,000 to ₹1,000 even though the click price stays identical. This is why quoting a CPC alone cannot tell a business what customer acquisition will cost.

Now apply your qualification and close rates. If you do not have those rates, mark them as unknown and plan a limited test. Avoid borrowing a successful account’s numbers without checking the product, location, sales cycle and tracking definition.

sections.title: Check what a daily budget actually means
body: Google describes the setting as an average daily budget. Its current guidance says a campaign can spend up to twice that average on a day, with the standard monthly limit based on 30.4 times the average. Check the rules that apply to your campaign and any budget changes before setting a limit. An average is not a promise of identical daily spending.

Keep enough visibility to catch unexpected pacing. Identify who checks spend, who can change the limit and when approval is required. An alert helps somebody notice a problem; it is not automatically a hard spending stop.

sections.title: Compare proposals by the work they cover
body: Ask whether keyword planning, ad copy, conversion testing, landing-page work and reporting are included. Check whether the quoted work stops after launch or includes ongoing search-term reviews. Domain, hosting, creative and third-party tool costs should be identifiable rather than hidden inside a vague ‘all-inclusive’ number.

For a new service business, a focused campaign with a working enquiry path can be more informative than launching many categories at once. ReddyStack uses a custom scope rather than publishing one advertising price for every industry. The proposal should explain what you are paying for and which costs remain with the platform.

title: Google Ads for Local Businesses
description: Build a Google Ads plan for a local business. Define service areas, choose useful searches, and connect ads to pages that turn interest into enquiries.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: A local-business Search campaign needs a clear service area, a reachable business and a page that answers the buyer’s immediate question. Start with the service you can fulfil reliably.

sections.title: Make geographic intent explicit
body: Write down towns, areas or travel boundaries that the business actually serves. Review location options and observed user locations after launch; a phrase containing a city name does not by itself guarantee every enquiry comes from that city.
bullets: List the services you want enquiries for and those you do not provide.
Match ads to relevant service pages with contact and availability information.
Align call handling and campaign schedules with the actual response process.
Define qualified outcomes, such as a suitable appointment or accepted quotation request.

sections.title: Use a local test brief
body: For an illustrative repair business: advertise one repair category within the agreed service boundary, explain the booking process and route enquiries to the person who can schedule work. Use a dedicated confirmation event for completed requests and treat a call-button click as a separate signal. Avoid claims such as “open now” or “same-day service” unless the business can fulfil them.

sections.title: Review the full enquiry path
body: Compare search terms, locations, calls, form submissions and accepted jobs. Ask why enquiries were declined: distance, unavailable service, price mismatch or missed contact. Feed those findings into the next targeting and copy revision. Scale only when the team can handle the extra work and the resulting jobs justify acquisition costs. Local visibility is valuable when it creates serviceable demand.

sections.title: Build the offer around work you can accept
body: List the jobs you want before writing keywords. An appliance technician might repair certain brands but not sell spare parts or offer training. Those boundaries belong in campaign planning and, where useful, on the destination page. Otherwise relevant-looking traffic can still create unusable enquiries.

Keep the area description practical. Travel time, appointment availability and minimum job value may matter more than a neat radius on a map. Use the actual service boundary and check the live account’s location options. A city name in an ad does not replace that check.

sections.title: Make the contact route fit the business day
body: If the main action is a phone call, confirm who answers it and what happens when they are busy. A click on the phone link is evidence of an attempt, not proof of a completed conversation. If the main action is a form, state what information helps arrange the next step and check that the request reaches the right person.

Avoid availability claims the business cannot fulfil. ‘Book a repair assessment’ creates a different expectation from ‘Technician at your door today’. Use the narrower claim when same-day availability changes with workload.

sections.title: Review the jobs, not just the leads
body: At the end of the test, separate enquiries by accepted job, outside area, wrong service, price mismatch and missed contact. Suppose most rejected leads are for spare parts: a service clarification and relevant exclusions may help more than a bid adjustment. If the right people call but nobody answers, repair call handling first.

Keep a record of revenue and direct job costs where available. A distant low-value job can be unprofitable after travel even when its lead price looks low. Expand coverage only when the economics and delivery capacity support it. This is a business decision informed by advertising data, not a target to maximise every enquiry count.

title: Google Ads Negative Keywords: A Review Workflow
description: Find and review negative keywords in Google Ads. Reduce irrelevant searches while avoiding exclusions that block potential customers.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Negative keywords help control irrelevant Search traffic, but an overly broad exclusion can also block suitable customers. Build exclusions from evidence and the business’s actual boundaries.

sections.title: Classify the search terms
body: Review the available search-term report alongside lead outcomes. Separate irrelevant searches from relevant searches that simply have not converted yet. The report may not expose every search, so avoid treating it as a complete record of demand.
bullets: Employment intent: jobs, salary or internships when recruiting is not the campaign goal.
Learning intent: tutorials or courses when the business only sells execution.
Wrong offering: products or services the business does not provide.
Wrong location: areas outside coverage, after checking how the phrase is used.

sections.title: Apply exclusions at the right scope
body: An illustrative agency may exclude “jobs” from a client-acquisition campaign while preserving it in a recruiting campaign. A store should not automatically exclude “free” if it advertises free delivery. Choose account, campaign or ad-group scope according to whether the exclusion is truly universal. Negative match behaviour differs from positive keyword matching; check the current platform rules before uploading a list.

sections.title: Maintain an exclusion log
body: Record the term, reason, scope and date. Revisit exclusions after expanding products or service areas. Review possible conflicts when valuable traffic drops suddenly. A maintained list is useful account knowledge; a huge downloaded list with no context is not evidence of good optimisation. Measure changes using relevant enquiries or sales, not only the reduction in total clicks.

sections.title: Use the full phrase to understand the intent
body: Words that look irrelevant in isolation can be valuable in context. ‘Free’ might describe a visitor expecting unpaid work, or a genuine buyer asking whether delivery is free. ‘Jobs’ might be employment intent, but it could appear in a business name or an industry-specific phrase. Read the complete available query and the offer before applying a blanket exclusion.

For an illustrative website agency, enquiries about courses and internships can be separated from businesses requesting a build. Keep examples of the rejected themes in your notes. That helps a future reviewer understand why the exclusion was added.

sections.title: Choose how widely the exclusion should apply
body: Use a broad account-level exclusion only when it is irrelevant to every affected campaign. A term that is wrong for one service may be useful for another. Campaign and ad-group decisions require the same care: an exclusion intended to route traffic can instead block it if the surrounding structure is misunderstood.

Negative keywords have their own matching rules. Check the current Google documentation for the selected negative match type rather than assuming it behaves like a positive keyword. Before uploading a large list, inspect a small sample and look for conflicts with your services, brands and best-performing queries.

sections.title: Give the list a maintenance routine
body: Keep the term, match type, scope, reason, owner and date in the change log. Review it when the business adds a product, location or service. A once-correct exclusion can become an accidental barrier after the offer changes.

After a material update, look at relevant enquiries, spend and useful query coverage. A fall in clicks alone is not evidence of success; you may have blocked valuable demand. Google also omits some low-volume searches from the report for privacy, so label the analysis as a review of the available terms rather than a complete account of every search.

title: Google Ads Conversion Tracking Checklist
description: Check Google Ads conversion tracking from the customer action to your CRM or order records. Test events and accuracy before using them for bidding.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Conversion tracking should record the business action that actually happened. Validate the journey from the customer’s device to the platform and your own records before using the event for bidding.

sections.title: Define each conversion
body: Create an event inventory with the outcome, trigger, source, value, currency and counting rule. Distinguish primary business goals from diagnostic events. Document whether an event is collected directly or imported so the same action is not accidentally counted twice.
bullets: Lead: successful accepted submission rather than merely opening the form.
Purchase: confirmed order with a transaction identifier and actual value.
Phone: distinguish a call-button click from a measured call outcome.
Offline sale: confirm identity matching, permission and the import process before use.

sections.title: Run a test matrix
body: Test mobile and desktop, successful and failed submissions, repeat clicks, refreshed confirmation pages and any cross-domain handoff. A successful test should appear in the business system exactly as expected. Reconcile it with the platform diagnostics after allowing for reporting delays. Check consent choices as part of the implementation; tracking must respect the visitor’s applicable choices.

sections.title: Make maintenance visible
body: Keep a record of the test, date and responsible owner. Retest after form, checkout, analytics or consent changes. If conversions abruptly disappear, compare the CRM or order system before assuming demand collapsed. Do not put personal information in page URLs or generic analytics event names. A reliable setup includes a way to detect failure, not only a one-time installation.

sections.title: Write an event definition somebody else can test
body: Use a sentence such as ‘Count a lead after the server accepts the enquiry and the user sees confirmation.’ Avoid ‘Track the contact form’, which leaves open whether the event fires on opening, clicking or successful delivery. Include the expected behaviour when validation fails, the network drops or the person presses the button twice.

For orders, define whether the value includes shipping, discounts and tax, then keep that convention consistent. Use the actual confirmed order identifier where the integration supports it. A random identifier generated on each page load cannot reliably identify a repeat view of the same order.

sections.title: Test both success and failure
body: Create a labelled test using the real route a customer takes. Confirm the business receives it, then inspect the analytics and advertising diagnostics. Test an invalid form and a failed payment too: neither should create the same success event. Check the effect of refreshing confirmation pages and returning through a payment-provider redirect.

Compare mobile and desktop and the relevant consent choices. Allow for the platform’s reporting delay before concluding that an absent report row means a broken tag. Record what was directly observed and what remains pending; installation status alone is not verification.

sections.title: Keep measurement separate from customer information
body: An event can describe the service requested or the success state without containing the message, phone number or email address. Do not put personal details in page URLs, event names or generic analytics parameters. Any eligible customer-data feature needs its own permissions and correctly configured data handling.

Retest after changes to forms, checkout, domains or consent tools. Assign an owner to compare successful business records with recorded events periodically. A sudden drop can be a website failure, a tracking failure or a real demand change; this comparison helps distinguish them before someone changes campaign budgets.

title: Google Ads Keyword Match Types Explained
description: Understand broad, phrase, and exact match in Google Ads. Compare reach and control, then use search-term reviews to refine your keyword strategy.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Broad, phrase and exact match provide different levels of reach and control. Match types describe how ads can become eligible for searches; they do not replace conversion measurement or search-term review.

sections.title: Understand the three options
body: Broad match can include related searches beyond the keyword’s direct wording. Phrase match considers searches that include the meaning of the keyword. Exact match can include the same meaning or intent, so it does not mean an exact character-for-character phrase. Google’s current documentation is the source for detailed matching behaviour.
bullets: Broad: assess whether bidding goals, conversion quality and budget can support wider discovery.
Phrase: inspect which related meanings reach the campaign.
Exact: use for tighter intent steering without assuming variants are impossible.

sections.title: Use a business example
body: For an illustrative business selling website development, “website development service” and searches about learning to build a website have different commercial implications. The relevant decision is whether the actual query fits the offer and produces qualified enquiries. Adding the same phrase in every match type does not automatically create more useful demand.

sections.title: Review after launch
body: Read the available search terms, campaign priorities and conversion outcomes. Investigate irrelevant themes and apply suitable negatives; negative match rules are different from positive match rules. Keep a change log and avoid judging a match type by one short period with few sales. The best setup is the one that reaches useful demand within your economics and operational limits.

sections.title: Think about meaning before punctuation
body: The brackets around an exact-match keyword do not make it a literal text comparison. Google describes exact matching in terms of the same meaning or intent, phrase matching around included meaning, and broad matching as wider related searches. That makes the actual search-term review important even when the keyword list looks tightly controlled.

Take an illustrative repair business advertising washing-machine repairs. A person seeking a technician, someone comparing a replacement machine and someone learning how to repair one have different needs. The useful question is which of those needs the offer can serve, not simply whether the query contains the words in your keyword.

sections.title: Match reach to measurement quality
body: Broader discovery gives a system more possible searches to consider. It also makes a dependable conversion goal and sensible spending plan especially important. Google recommends Smart Bidding with broad match. Before using any setup, confirm that the goal represents an outcome the business actually values and that duplicated or trivial events are not distorting it.

A small business with very limited outcome data should treat conclusions cautiously. One lead does not establish that a match type works, and one irrelevant search does not establish that every broader term should be removed. Review themes, spending and suitable outcomes together.

sections.title: Make changes you can interpret
body: Keep a dated record of the keyword, match type and reason for the change. If you simultaneously change bidding, geography, creative and the landing page, it becomes difficult to tell what caused the result. Separate obvious exclusions from experiments intended to discover new demand.

When the business expands its offer, revisit old negatives and the destination pages. A previously irrelevant query may now be suitable. Match types are one control within the campaign; a clear offer, functioning enquiry path and maintained exclusions remain part of the same job.

intro: A paid-search landing page should continue the promise made in the ad and make the next step work on a phone. Use this checklist before launch and after material changes.

sections.title: Check message and decision information
body: Open the destination from the ad preview where possible. A visitor should understand what is offered, who it fits and what happens after enquiry without decoding vague slogans.
bullets: Headline and ad describe the same service or offer.
Inclusions, important exclusions and applicable pricing context are visible.
Proof is relevant and approved for public use.
Contact and business identity are easy to find.
Primary form or checkout works with clear labels and errors.
The page loads without a blocking overlay or unusable mobile controls.

sections.title: Test the conversion path
body: Submit a clearly marked test enquiry with realistic validation, then confirm delivery to the responsible person. Test a failure case and repeated submission as well. Check that measurement counts the successful action, preserves necessary campaign information and avoids putting personal data in URLs. A thank-you message on screen is not proof that the business received the enquiry.

sections.title: Choose the next experiment
body: If visitors understand the offer but abandon the form, inspect the required fields and errors. If enquiries are consistently unsuitable, improve eligibility and expectations before removing all friction. Compare qualified outcomes alongside conversion rate. Keep accessibility, readable contrast and keyboard operation in every version; a visually simpler page should still work for the people expected to use it.

sections.title: Answer the questions before asking for contact details
body: A visitor should be able to identify the service, the area covered, the main inclusions and the next step. If price depends on scope, explain which inputs affect it. If a starting price covers only a limited version, put the boundary close to that price. Do not make a buyer submit a form just to discover that the advertised offer does not apply.

Use relevant proof. A screenshot of a finished website can demonstrate development work, but it does not establish that an advertising campaign produced sales. Label demonstrations and personal projects honestly, and describe what the reader can actually inspect.

sections.title: Test with a phone and an imperfect connection
body: Open the real destination, not only a design preview. Read it with the keyboard open, tap the contact action and correct an invalid field. Check whether error messages tell you what to change and whether entered text survives a temporary failure. If a sticky element covers the action, the conversion path needs repair before more traffic is sent.

Confirm that links lead to the intended pages after redirects. Keep the ad’s promise visible near the top and make the page understandable without waiting for an animation. Accessibility checks such as visible labels, readable contrast and keyboard operation also expose common usability problems.

sections.title: Measure the action the business receives
body: Record successful accepted enquiries separately from button clicks. A visitor can click WhatsApp and never send a message; a form can display a success state while delivery fails. Use the available business record to verify what the event means.

When reviewing a test, track enquiry suitability as well as submission rate. Removing every qualification field may increase volume but create more unserviceable requests. Make one change with a stated purpose, keep the before version and allow enough time for the sales outcome you are assessing.

title: Improve Lead Quality from Google Ads
description: Poor Google Ads lead quality can come from mismatched search intent, targeting, the offer or the sales process. Diagnose rejected enquiries before changing bids or adding budget.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: Poor Google Ads lead quality can come from mismatched search intent, targeting, the offer or the sales process. Diagnose rejected enquiries before changing bids or adding budget.

sections.title: Give rejection reasons names
body: Review a representative sample with the person who handles enquiries. Mark duplicates, wrong service, outside coverage, wrong budget, uncontactable and qualified. Record response timing so a missed call is not automatically blamed on targeting.
bullets: Wrong service: compare search terms and ad-group themes with the landing page.
Wrong geography: inspect location settings and observed customer locations.
Research-only interest: clarify the service and commercial next step.
Uncontactable: check validation, duplicate records and response handling.

sections.title: Optimise for a meaningful outcome
body: Illustrative comparison: two campaigns spend ₹8,000 each. One produces 40 enquiries with four qualified; the other produces 20 with eight qualified. The second campaign has the lower qualified-lead cost despite its higher raw CPL. If feasible, plan measurement of qualified outcomes with appropriate permissions and data handling. Do not blindly change the bidding goal to an untested event.

sections.title: Run a focused correction
body: Choose one cause supported by the data, such as an irrelevant query theme or an unclear minimum scope. Update the relevant negative keywords, copy or qualification question and review both enquiry volume and suitability. Avoid claiming improved quality merely because fewer people submit. The end point is more useful customer conversations at a sustainable acquisition cost.

sections.title: Trace one rejected lead back to its promise
body: Choose a recent unsuitable enquiry and compare the customer’s request with the ad and destination page. Where available, review its search context. If the person wanted a product you do not sell, check the campaign theme. If they expected a much lower price, look for a misleading starting price or missing scope explanation.

Do the same for a suitable enquiry. Comparing the two can reveal a practical distinction, such as commercial versus residential work, rather than a vague belief that the audience is wrong. Keep customer information out of shared screenshots unless its use is authorised.

sections.title: Fix the specific mismatch
body: For wrong-service enquiries, clarify the offer and review related search terms. For outside-area requests, inspect the account’s location configuration and actual lead locations. For people who cannot be contacted, inspect contact validation and response handling. Each diagnosis suggests a different correction.

A useful qualifier asks for information that changes whether you can serve the person. A requirement type or postcode may help; an unnecessary long questionnaire may simply discourage genuine buyers. State important boundaries in the copy before adding form friction.

sections.title: Measure quality consistently over time
body: Define ‘qualified’ in plain language and have the people handling leads use the same rule. Record response time and pending outcomes. If one salesperson marks every unanswered call as rejected while another continues following up, their campaign comparison will be unreliable.

Use qualified-lead cost and completed customer outcomes alongside raw CPL. If the business later imports qualified outcomes into advertising tools, validate the matching, permissions and duplicate handling first. An untested new bidding signal can create a different measurement problem rather than solve the original one.

title: Google Ads Budget Planning Worksheet
description: A Google Ads budget is a model of demand and conversion economics. Write the assumptions down so you can change the plan when real results disagree with it.
subtitle: Google Ads guides · ReddyStack · Updated 22 September 2026
intro: A Google Ads budget is a model of demand and conversion economics. Write the assumptions down so you can change the plan when real results disagree with it.

sections.title: Collect the inputs
body: Use your own historical results where possible. Otherwise label the numbers as assumptions and create a range rather than a single confident forecast.
bullets: Affordable acquisition cost per new customer.
Estimated cost per click for the market and intent.
Expected click-to-enquiry or click-to-purchase rate.
Qualification and close rates for lead generation.
Maximum test spend, production costs and review responsibility.

sections.title: Work through an illustrative model
body: Assume ₹30 CPC, a 5% enquiry rate, 50% qualification and a 20% close rate among qualified leads. One thousand clicks cost ₹30,000 and imply 50 enquiries, 25 qualified leads and five customers. Media acquisition cost is ₹6,000 per customer. This is arithmetic based on assumptions, not a prediction. Re-run the sheet with weaker conversion rates to see the downside.

sections.title: Connect planning to controls
body: Allocate spend to distinct business goals and confirm campaign budget rules in the live account. Review spend pacing, conversion delays and capacity before increasing limits. Keep fees and media separate and obtain approval for meaningful scope changes. If the economics cannot work under realistic assumptions, revisit the offer, margins or landing journey before trying to solve the problem with more budget.

sections.title: Stress-test the numbers before spending
body: Take the model above and halve the enquiry rate from 5% to 2.5%, leaving the other assumptions unchanged. The same 1,000 clicks then imply 25 enquiries, 12.5 qualified leads and 2.5 customers as planning averages. Media acquisition cost doubles from ₹6,000 to ₹12,000. Real outcomes are whole people; fractional results here simply describe the average implied by the assumptions.

Ask whether the business can afford that weaker result. Include management, creative and landing-page costs separately. A campaign that only works under the most optimistic close rate needs a better plan before it needs a larger budget.

sections.title: Check demand and capacity
body: A budget is permission to spend, not proof that enough suitable demand exists. Use available planning estimates and your own account history to assess the market. A narrow local service may have limited relevant searches; an overly broad campaign may find volume without finding suitable customers.

Also check delivery capacity. If a business can accept only a few new jobs, plan around that limit and its sales cycle. The ability to answer and fulfil enquiries is part of the budget decision. More clicks are not helpful when every suitable lead is told to wait indefinitely.

sections.title: Agree the operating rules
body: Name the person who checks spend, the point at which the test is reviewed and the changes that require approval. Record the campaign budget setting and the platform’s current spending rules. Keep alerts and reporting separate from any actual spending controls; an email alert does not itself stop a campaign.

At review, update the assumptions with observed data and show which values remain uncertain. Keep pending sales visible rather than treating them as losses too early. Choose the next step from the economics: continue a focused test, repair a specific problem, change the offer or stop spending on an unworkable combination.

title: Google Ads Reporting Metrics and Decisions
description: A Google Ads report should connect the search campaign to customer outcomes. State the reporting window and conversion definitions before interpreting changes.

intro: A Google Ads report should connect the search campaign to customer outcomes. State the reporting window and conversion definitions before interpreting changes.

sections.title: Build three reporting layers
body: Delivery explains what was purchased; conversion explains the recorded actions; business results explain whether those actions were useful. Keep all three instead of elevating one metric to a universal score.
bullets: Delivery: spend, impressions, clicks, CPC and relevant coverage indicators.
Conversion: defined actions, conversion rate, cost per action and reported value.
Business: unique enquiries, qualified leads, new customers and verified revenue.
Context: budget changes, promotions, tracking changes and conversion delays.

sections.title: Read ratios together
body: Illustrative example: CPC rises from ₹20 to ₹30 while the purchase rate rises from 2% to 5%. Media cost per purchase changes from ₹1,000 to ₹600 despite more expensive clicks. Conversely, cheaper clicks can increase customer cost if intent becomes weaker. Use consistent date ranges and avoid comparing a partial current week with a complete previous week.

sections.title: End with a decision
body: Write a short statement connecting evidence to the next action: “spend increased in an unserviceable area; review location settings and lead rejection records.” Record who will act and how the change will be checked. Platform attribution and analytics can differ, so reconcile important sales in the business system rather than silently presenting conflicting totals as equivalent.

sections.title: Separate a business result from a platform signal
body: A click, a contact-button tap, an accepted enquiry and a completed sale describe different events. Put each in the appropriate row. Calling all of them conversions without explaining the definition makes the report appear more decisive than it is.

For lead generation, keep a simple sequence: unique enquiries, qualified enquiries, quotations and customers. Show unresolved leads as pending. A business with a long buying cycle needs time to complete this sequence, so compare sufficiently mature groups of leads when assessing close rate.

sections.title: Investigate a change before celebrating it
body: Suppose the reported cost per conversion falls after a new event is imported. Check whether the system is now counting an easier action or duplicating the old one. If clicks rise but suitable enquiries do not, inspect search themes, destinations and the offer before calling the extra traffic growth.

Use annotations for budget changes, new services, promotions, website repairs and tracking releases. Those notes make a future comparison possible. Keep the original reporting range and definitions so a revised report does not quietly change what last month’s figures meant.

sections.title: Make the report short enough to act on
body: Include the question being answered, the relevant numbers and the next action. ‘Outside-area enquiries increased after coverage changed; review location settings and the landing-page boundary’ gives someone a task. A page of dashboard screenshots may not.

Keep detailed exports available for investigation, but lead the summary with customer outcomes and material uncertainty. Google Ads, Analytics and business records can use different attribution and timing conventions. Reconcile important sales rather than forcing those systems to display identical daily totals or adding their counts together.
